intro: To contrast two ideas, “but” is not always enough. “Although”, “however” and “despite” let you express contrast in a more precise way, in speech and in writing. But each one has its own grammar: a clause, a noun or a separate sentence.
objectifs: Use although / though / even though + subject + verb.
Use despite / in spite of + noun, + -ing or + the fact that.
Place however and nevertheless correctly, with the right punctuation.
Change a sentence from one structure to another without changing the meaning.

texte: All these words express contrast: the second idea is surprising or unexpected compared with the first. The difference is grammatical: what comes after the word.
A very common mistake is “despite of”: it does not exist. Say “despite” or “in spite of”.

lignes: It was raining, but we went out.
Although it was raining, we went out.
Even though it was raining, we went out.
Despite the rain, we went out.
It was raining. However, we went out.
It was raining. Nevertheless, we went out.

texte: These conjunctions introduce a full clause (subject + verb). They can go at the start of the sentence (followed by a comma) or in the middle.

“Though” is more common in speech. “Even though” makes the contrast stronger and is used for real facts. In speech, “though” can also go at the end of a sentence, meaning “however”: “It was expensive. I bought it, though.”
Be careful: don't use “but” in the same sentence as although (“Although it was late, but…” is wrong).
exemples: Although she was tired, she finished the report.
I enjoyed the trip to Kinshasa, though it was very hot.
Even though he earns a lot, he never has any money.
The hotel was nice. The food wasn't great, though.

texte: “Despite” and “in spite of” have exactly the same meaning. They are followed by a noun, a pronoun or a verb-ing, never directly by a clause.
To add a full clause, use “despite the fact that” / “in spite of the fact that” + subject + verb. Never write “despite of”.

lignes: Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.
In spite of his age, he still plays football.
Despite feeling ill, she went to work.
Despite the fact that it was late, the shop was open.

exemples: We enjoyed the evening despite the rain.
despite + noun, in the middle of the sentence.
In spite of working hard, he didn't get a promotion.

sections.titre: However and nevertheless: linking two sentences
texte: “However” is a linking adverb: it connects two separate sentences, not two clauses inside one sentence. It usually starts the second sentence, followed by a comma; it can also go in the middle, between commas.
Inside one sentence, you can use a semicolon: “It was raining; however, we went out.” But “It was raining, however we went out” (with only a comma) is considered incorrect in writing.
“Nevertheless” and “nonetheless” mean the same but are more formal: they suit reports and professional emails.
exemples: The project was difficult. However, the team finished it on time.
The new phone is expensive. It is, however, very fast.
however in the middle, between commas.
Sales fell in March; nevertheless, the company made a profit.

sections.titre: Changing from one structure to another
texte: It is very useful (and common in exams) to change from one structure to another. With despite, find a noun or an -ing form that matches the verb: “it rained” → “the rain”; “he was ill” → “his illness” / “being ill”.

lignes: Although he was ill, he came.
He was ill. However, he came.
Although she has a lot of experience, she didn't get the job.
Despite her experience, she didn't get the job.
She has a lot of experience. However, she didn't get the job.

formule: although / even though + subject + verb · despite / in spite of + noun / -ing · Sentence 1. However, sentence 2.
prononciation: “although” /ɔːlˈðəʊ/: stress on the second syllable, voiced th /ð/, silent gh.
“though” /ðəʊ/ rhymes with “go”; don't confuse it with “through” /θruː/ or “thought” /θɔːt/.
“however” /haʊˈevə/: stress on the second syllable; in speech, make a short pause after it: However, | we…
At the end of a sentence, “though” has a fall-rise tone: It was good, though.
erreurs: Despite of the rain, we went out.
Despite the rain, we went out. / In spite of the rain, we went out.
despite without of; in spite of with of.
Although it was late, but we continued.
Although it was late, we continued.
No but with although.
Despite it was raining, we played.
Although it was raining, we played. / Despite the rain, we played.
despite + noun / -ing, not a clause.
It was expensive, however I bought it.
It was expensive. However, I bought it. / It was expensive, but I bought it.
however links two sentences (full stop or semicolon).
Although the traffic, we arrived on time.
Despite the traffic, we arrived on time.
Before a noun alone: despite.
In spite of be tired, he worked.
In spite of being tired, he worked.
After in spite of: -ing.
Even she was ill, she came.
Even though she was ill, she came.
even alone is not a conjunction: even though.

dialogue.contexte: Two friends, Didier and Sandrine, talk in Liège about Didier's new job.
lignes: I like it, although the hours are long.
Do you have to commute every day?
Yes. Despite the distance, it only takes forty minutes by train.
Most are great. My manager is quite strict. However, she's always fair.
And the salary? You didn't seem sure about it.
It's lower than at my old job. I'm much happier, though.
That's what matters. Even though money is important, it's not everything.

mots: Although it was cold, we swam.
Despite the noise, I slept well.
It's cheap. However, it's not very good.
It was risky. Nevertheless, they did it.
There's a big contrast between the two cities.
I commute to Brussels every day.
to travel regularly between home and work
My manager is strict but fair.
the money you earn from a job, paid every month
Despite her experience, she didn't get the job.
knowledge and skill from doing something

items: ___ the bad weather, the match went ahead.
Despite
___ he studied hard, he failed the exam.
Although
The hotel was cheap. ___, it was very clean.
However
She went to work ___ having a headache.
despite
___ I don't like football, I watched the final.
Although
The plan is good. It is, ___, very expensive.
however

exercices.consigne: Complete with the correct form after despite / in spite of (noun or -ing).
items: Despite ___ (be) very young, she runs her own company.
being
In spite of ___ (the / delay), we caught our connection.
the delay
Despite ___ (not / speak) French, he found a job in Quebec.
not speaking
Despite ___ fact that it was Sunday, the shop was open.
the

exercices.consigne: Rewrite with the word in brackets. Keep the same meaning.
items: Although it was raining, they had a picnic. (despite)
Despite the rain, they had a picnic.
Despite being tired, he went out. (although)
Although he was tired, he went out.
The car is old, but it works well. (however)
The car is old. However, it works well.
She didn't get the job although she had good qualifications. (in spite of)
She didn't get the job in spite of her good qualifications / in spite of having good qualifications.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: Despite of the cost, we bought the house.
Despite the cost, we bought the house.
Although he was rich, but he wasn't happy.
Although he was rich, he wasn't happy.
Despite she was ill, she came to the meeting.
Although she was ill, she came to the meeting. / Despite being ill, she came to the meeting.
Even I was late, they waited for me.
Even though I was late, they waited for me.

exercices.consigne: Join the two ideas with the word in brackets.
items: There was a strike. I was able to get to work. (despite)
Despite the strike, I was able to get to work.
He is shy. He gave an excellent speech. (although)
Although he is shy, he gave an excellent speech.
The restaurant was expensive. The meal was delicious. (however)
The restaurant was expensive. However, the meal was delicious.

exercices.consigne: Write a short paragraph (5 sentences) about the good and bad points of your town or job, with although, even though, despite and however.
items: Model answer

I love living in Douala, although the traffic is terrible. Despite the heat, there's always a nice breeze in the evening near the river. Rent is quite high. However, food is still affordable at the local markets. Even though I sometimes miss the calm of my village, I wouldn't move.

a_retenir: although / though / even though + subject + verb (Although it rained, …).
despite / in spite of + noun or -ing (Despite the rain / Despite being tired); never “despite of”.
however / nevertheless: at the start of the second sentence + comma, or after a semicolon.
No but with although; “though” at the end of a sentence = however (spoken).
